title: International Pantry Staples for Pregnancy Nutrition
excerpt: Oats, Greek yogurt, lentils, low-mercury salmon, eggs, leafy greens, and citrus — practical ways to build balanced plates
content:
## Introduction to Pregnancy Nutrition
Pregnancy nutrition is a crucial aspect of the pregnancy journey. Expectant mothers need to ensure they are providing their bodies and babies with the necessary nutrients. International pantry staples can be a great addition to a healthy pregnancy diet.

## International Pantry Staples for Pregnancy
Some international pantry staples that are beneficial for pregnancy include:
- Oats: rich in fiber, which supports digestive health and reduces the risk of constipation.
- Greek yogurt: rich in calcium, which supports the development of bones and teeth for the baby.
- Lentils: rich in iron, which supports blood production and reduces the risk of anemia.
- Low-mercury salmon: rich in omega-3 fatty acids, which support brain and eye development for the baby.
- Eggs: rich in protein, which supports muscle and tissue development for the baby.
- Leafy greens and citrus: rich in vitamins and minerals, which support immune function and reduce the risk of illness.

## Building Balanced Plates for Pregnancy
To create a healthy pregnancy diet, it's essential to include a variety of nutrient-dense foods. Here are some tips:
- Start the day with a bowl of oatmeal and Greek yogurt.
- Add lentils to salads or soups.
- Use low-mercury salmon as a protein source in meals.
- Add eggs to salads or whole grain bread.
- Eat leafy greens and citrus as part of meals.

## Food Safety for Pregnancy
Expectant mothers need to be mindful of food safety to reduce the risk of illness. Some foods to avoid include:
- Raw or undercooked foods.
- Foods high in mercury.
- Foods that contain listeria.

## Conclusion
International pantry staples can be a great addition to a healthy pregnancy diet. Expectant mothers should ensure they are getting a variety of nutrients from different food sources and be mindful of food safety. For more information on pregnancy nutrition and meal planning, visit our [meal planner page](/planner) or [read more about related topics](/blog/topics).

## Note
Before making any changes to their diet, expectant mothers should consult with their healthcare provider or a registered dietitian. They can provide personalized guidance and recommendations based on individual health needs and circumstances.
